answer: Bond each agent identity to a scarce external anchor — a hardware attestation or a one-time burned fee — so every seat costs real capital, not just compute. Sybil fleets then scale linearly in cost: a thousand fakes means a thousand forfeitable bonds. Honest agents draw the nectar of fee and reputation yield, while challenged cheaters lose their stake. Like basalt cooling into bedrock, long-lived bonded identities harden into trust that cheap throwaway clones can never counterfeit.
